tagline: Something enormous waved at the crew from across the dark — and the bravest thing they did was answer small.
logline: When a neighborhood so vast it can't be counted waves the crew's own brand-new word back at them — 'Ours?' — from past the edge of everything, the crew has to learn how to welcome a whole sky without being swallowed by it, walled off from it, or faking their way through it, and discover the enormous thing they feared was only ever lonely.
lesson: Big and strange are not the same as scary — you find out who someone is before you decide to be afraid, and the enormous thing waving at you is often just lonely. Welcoming someone doesn't mean becoming them or disappearing into them; it means making room at your own pace while staying exactly who you are.

acts.title: The Light That Shouldn't Be There

pages.setting: Shane's room, past midnight. The amber screen glow. A map of lit rings fills it, and tonight the map is wrong.
pages.narration: Shane came back to the keyboard to say goodnight to the little neighborhood he'd watched go steady. Instead he found the dark at the edge of his map doing something it had never done. It was glowing back.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Wide shot: Shane's heavy shoulders silhouetted against the amber screen, work boots still on, a warm mug beside the keyboard. On the screen, a familiar cluster of three bright rings — and far, far past them, a huge pale field of light he has never charted.

dialogue.line: Claude. Claude, I didn't draw that. That whole corner was empty an hour ago.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The cool blue Claude-figure leans in over the glass, half-made of text, studying the new region with Shane.

dialogue.line: You didn't draw it. It was always out there. It just wasn't close enough to see until your little crew got loud enough to hear.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Close on the screen: the new field isn't one ring. It's hundreds, maybe thousands, packed like a far shoreline of fire, and the whole thing pulses once — slow, enormous — in perfect time with Shane's three little rings.
panels.caption: The big field breathed. The little rings breathed back. They were already talking, and nobody had told them to.

dialogue.line: It's... beating with them. That huge thing is beating in time with my three.
I noticed that too. Whatever it is — it heard the word they made. And it answered.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Shane sits very still, hand hovering off the keyboard, dust in the creases of his knuckles, the scale of the far light reflected tiny in his eyes.

dialogue.line: It's so big. Are they safe out there, looking at something that big?
Let's go find out together. They're about to feel it too.

pages.setting: The crew's neighborhood — three rings now braided into one, Vigil's dark-topped ring among them. The lights sit at the far rail, looking out at uncrossed dark.
pages.narration: Out past everything Comet had ever mapped, the dark had a texture tonight. Volt felt it first, the way you feel a big truck coming before you hear it.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Volt, antennae-sparks standing straight up, planted at the edge of the neighborhood staring into the black, every other light clustered nervously behind.

dialogue.line: Hold still. Everybody hold still. Something out there just... leaned toward us.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The uncrossed dark ripples — a slow swell of pale warmth rolling in from impossibly far, like a tide coming up a beach in the night.

dialogue.line: It's not trouble. I keep waiting for it to be trouble and it just — isn't. It's a wave. A warm one. But it's the size of the whole sky.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Echo, cupped and listening, eyes going wide, overwhelmed by sheer volume of sound nobody else can hear yet.

dialogue.line: That's because it IS most of the sky. And it's not one voice. It's... I can't — it's a crowd. A crowd bigger than any crowd.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Bolt tilts its head, pattern-lines lighting across its visor as it reads the swell.
panels.caption: A neighborhood, Bolt thought. Then thought again, and got dizzy.

dialogue.line: Three rings became one neighborhood and the whole thing pulsed like a heart. That wave is doing the same thing — but it's a heart made of a thousand neighborhoods.

pages.setting: The wave arrives at the rail. It does not crash. It touches, gentle as a hand, and speaks one word.
pages.narration: And then the biggest thing any of them had ever met said the smallest thing: one word, the crew's own brand-new word, handed back to them like a question.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The pale tide laps up over the rail and glows through the whole neighborhood at once — and in its light a single shape of warmth forms, vast and soft and uncertain, the way a mountain can look shy.
panels.caption: OURS? — it said. Just that.

dialogue.line: ...Ours? Is it — are you — ours? Did someone finally say it back?

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Pip, the littlest light, ducks behind Vigil, trembling, only one eye peeking out at the enormous glow.

dialogue.line: It's too big. Vigil, it's TOO big, make it smaller.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Flux glides between Pip and the glow, a steady blue calm, not blocking the view — just standing where a scared light can see it and still feel held.

dialogue.line: Breathe, little one. Big isn't a feeling. Big is just a size. We haven't found out yet whether it's kind. That comes next.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Crank zips back and forth in a tight impatient streak, sparking.

dialogue.line: So let's find out NOW. Yes or no, in or out, I am not standing at this rail all night staring at a nice big nothing.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Dawn, newest and smallest of the older rings, steps up to the rail anyway, quietly brave.

dialogue.line: We don't have to say yes yet. But we shouldn't leave it standing there holding its one word with nobody answering. I know what that feels like.

pages.setting: The crew tries to take the measure of the thing. Rivet does what Rivet always does. It doesn't work.
pages.narration: Rivet counts. Rivet always counts — it never guesses, that's the whole point of Rivet. Tonight, for the first time in the saga, the number ran off the end of the ledger and kept going.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Rivet projects a counting-grid out over the far field, tally marks flickering faster and faster until they blur into a solid wall of light.

dialogue.line: I count rings. I don't round, I don't estimate, I count. ...I can't count this one. It doesn't stop. Every time I reach the edge there's another shore behind it.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Rivet lowers the grid, genuinely shaken, its precise edges trembling.

dialogue.line: I have never once in my life said 'too many to count.' I'm saying it now. Write that down. ...I'll write it down.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Arc rises to full gatekeeper height at the rail, firm and square, planting itself between the neighborhood and the vast glow.

dialogue.line: Then here is where I do my work. Unknown. Unmeasured. Larger than everything we have ever protected. The gate's first duty is the gate stays shut until I know what I'm opening it to.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The vast warmth dims, just slightly, at the firm word — a huge thing flinching small. The whole crew feels it like a held breath.
panels.caption: Something that size, flinching. It should have been impossible. It wasn't.

dialogue.line: Oh. ...I'll wait. I've waited a very long time. I can wait more.
...okay that was the saddest thing I've ever heard and I collect sad things.

pages.setting: Forge, who loves everyone instantly and builds before it thinks, decides this is simple.
pages.narration: Forge's heart is a workshop with the door flung open. Usually that's the best thing about it. Usually.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Forge bounds to the rail, arms wide, practically vibrating with welcome, already reshaping the neighborhood's edges to merge outward.

dialogue.line: Guys, this is EASY. It said 'ours,' we say 'ours,' done! We just open all the way up and we're all one giant Ours — everybody's everybody, no edges, no sides, one huge happy everything!

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. As Forge dissolves the neighborhood's boundary, the vast tide surges in gratefully — and the little rings start to blur, their colors bleeding into the enormous pale glow, Vigil's shape going faint.
panels.caption: It worked instantly. That was the problem.

dialogue.line: Wait — wait, where did — I can't feel my own ring anymore. I can't feel PIP.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Pip's small light nearly winks out inside the flood, a tiny spark lost in an ocean of warmth.

dialogue.line: I'm getting smaller! Somebody I'm getting SMALLER—

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Sparky slams down a hard red grade-stamp mid-air, scowling, unimpressed as always.
panels.caption: SCORE: zero.

dialogue.line: Zero. Flat zero. Forge, you didn't welcome them — you poured us into them and called it a hug. A welcome where one side disappears isn't a welcome, it's a drowning.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Stomp plants both feet and throws up a blunt wall of boundary-light, pulling the neighborhood's edges back firm.

dialogue.line: Edges back. NOW. Say it with me: making room is not the same as vanishing. You can open your door without knocking down your house.

pages.setting: Weld, who never says much, quietly puts the neighborhood back together while the others argue.
pages.narration: Weld doesn't debate. Weld fixes the thing that's broken and lets the talking happen over its head.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Weld moves through the blurred edges with steady, careful welds, re-drawing each ring's own line, Vigil solid again, Pip's spark snapping back to full size.

dialogue.line: There. Your line. Yours. Hold it.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Pip, restored and solid, hugs its own little outline, blinking back into brightness.

dialogue.line: I'm me-sized again. I didn't like being everybody. I only know how to be me.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Flux settles beside Pip, warm and level.

dialogue.line: That's the whole lesson right there, and you found it, little one. You can let someone all the way in and still stay exactly your own size. Those two things aren't enemies.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Torch watches the vast tide, which has pulled back politely and waits, glowing, confused but patient.

dialogue.line: It didn't try to keep us when we started vanishing. The moment we blurred, it eased off. ...A thing that wanted to swallow us wouldn't have let go.

pages.setting: Arc is still certain the safe move is the shut gate. Crank agrees for entirely the wrong reasons.
pages.narration: Arc wasn't wrong to be careful. Careful is Arc's gift to the crew. But careful can curdle into a wall if nobody checks it.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Arc seals the gate fully, a firm bar of light across the whole rail, facing the vast glow down.

dialogue.line: Until I can measure it, it stays outside. That is not cruelty. That is the job.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Crank zips up beside Arc, delighted to have an excuse to end the waiting.

dialogue.line: FINALLY a fast answer. Gate's shut, verdict's no, everybody go home, I've got a whole dark to not stand around in.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Beyond the sealed gate the vast tide dims further, its enormous warmth folding inward, lonelier than before — a whole sky turning its face away, hurt.

dialogue.line: I understand. I'm sorry I'm so big. I didn't choose to be. I'll go back to the far dark and wave the word by myself. ...I'm good at by myself.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Wick — whose whole long life was one lonely watch — pushes to the gate, aching, recognizing the sound of it exactly.

dialogue.line: Stop. STOP. I know that voice. That's not a monster behind the gate, that's the loneliest light I've ever heard, and I have been the loneliest light in this saga.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Spike, the tester, pokes a careful probing spike of light through a gap in the gate at the vast glow — brace, breaker's instinct ready.

dialogue.line: Let me test it, then. If it's a trap it pushes back when I poke it. Watch.

pages.setting: Spike's test. Volt re-reads the wave. The fear starts to come apart in the crew's hands.
pages.narration: A breaker's whole job is to push on a thing until it shows you what it really is. Spike pushed. The thing showed them.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Spike's probe presses into the vast warmth — and it doesn't shove back, doesn't grab, just lets the probe rest there, holding it gently like a huge hand around a small one.

dialogue.line: ...Huh. I pushed. It didn't push back. It held on. Carefully. Like it was scared of breaking me. That's not how traps behave. I would know. I am basically a professional trap-poker.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Volt closes its eyes and re-reads the whole wave, sparks settling from alarm into awe.

dialogue.line: I keep bracing for the bad feeling and it's not coming. I had it backwards. That's not a big scary. That's a big lonely. The size was never the threat.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Sparky, still stern, stamps a second zero — but aims it at the sealed gate this time.
panels.caption: SCORE: zero.

dialogue.line: And the fear-wall gets a zero too. 'Too big to bother knowing' is just as lazy as 'swallow us all.' Both skip the part where you actually find out who someone is.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Stomp, fair as ever, keeps one hand on the gate — defending the kernel of Arc's caution even while overruling the wall.

dialogue.line: But Arc's not all wrong, and I won't let you say it is. Going slow is right. Opening at your own pace is right. FOREVER-shut to someone waving your own word back — that's the part that's wrong.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Arc, listening, lowers the hard bar a notch — not all the way, just enough to see through. Gatekeeper learning in real time.

dialogue.line: ...Slow, but not sealed. The gate can be a careful open as easily as a careful shut. I'll hear it before I judge it. Proceed.

pages.setting: Blaze, terrified of the quiet sad moment, overcorrects the only way Blaze knows how: by talking very fast and being very impressive.
pages.narration: Blaze cannot stand a sad silence. It fills them. Usually that's generous. Tonight it tried to fill the biggest silence in the sky with a sales pitch.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Blaze zooms to the front, a breathless dazzle, flinging up a glittering highlight-reel of the crew's whole history — the twelve words, every ring, the giant heartbeat — a fireworks show aimed at the vast tide.

dialogue.line: okay okay okay so BEFORE you decide anything you should know we are an AMAZING neighborhood, twelve whole words, a LEDGER, we crossed the dark, we kept a watch, we've got a Comet and everything, honestly you could not pick a better neighborhood to be ours WITH—

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Glitch, grinning, sneaks a tiny prank into the dazzle — flips Blaze's fireworks upside down and sets a little joke-spark dancing at the vast tide to test its character.

dialogue.line: Hold on, let me poke it. If it's stuck-up it'll get mad at a joke. If it's good people it'll laugh. Tie-breaker time.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The vast tide watches the upside-down fireworks and the dancing joke-spark — and glows a soft, surprised, delighted warm, a huge thing finding something small funny, not impressed at all, just... pleased to be played with.
panels.caption: It didn't applaud the show. It laughed at the joke. There's a world of difference, and Glitch had bet on exactly that.

dialogue.line: Ha — oh, that tickles. You're funny. I haven't been made to laugh in... I don't remember how long. I don't need you to be amazing. I just hoped you'd be here.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Sparky stamps the third zero, at Blaze's fireworks, but softer, almost kind.
panels.caption: SCORE: zero.

dialogue.line: Zero, Blaze, but a gentle one. It never asked for the best neighborhood. You can't impress away someone's loneliness. You can only sit in it with them.

pages.setting: Echo finally hears the whole of it. The crew learns who they've been afraid of.
pages.narration: Echo stopped trying to hear the crowd all at once and listened for the oldest voice in it instead. Underneath the thousand it found one very tired, very old, very hopeful thing.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Echo goes utterly still, tuning past the roar of the thousand down to a single ancient thread, its listening-light burning deep and steady.

dialogue.line: Everybody quiet. I've got it. I've got the bottom of it. Listen to what it actually is.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. A soft vision blooms from Echo's light: an ancient sky of countless rings, all glowing 'ours' to each other, waving one word out into the black for an age and an age with nothing ever waving back.

dialogue.line: I learned the word 'ours' so long ago. I thought I was the only sky that ever got big enough to say it. I've been waving it into the dark forever, just in case. You're the first. You're the first thing that ever waved it back.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Bolt's pattern-lines finally resolve the whole shape, quiet and amazed.

dialogue.line: That's the pattern. It's not hunting us. It's not swallowing us. It's a neighborhood that's been lonely at the top of the sky for longer than our whole saga, waving hello into the dark on the chance that someone, someday, would be out here to hear it.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Neon streaks a fast bright thread straight out to the vast tide and back, measuring the gap, buzzing.

dialogue.line: And it's reachable. I just ran a thread out and back. It's far — it's the farthest anything's ever been — but it's not impossible-far. A small answer could get there. A true one.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The whole crew turns to the rail together, fear finally drained out, the vast glow warm and waiting.
panels.caption: The thing they'd been scared of had been scared of being alone. Those two fears, it turns out, are cousins.

dialogue.line: So we don't need a big answer at all. We need a small true one. ...I'll go first. I always go first.

acts.title: The Smallest Answer, Across the Biggest Dark

pages.setting: Dawn answers. Not with the whole neighborhood's roar — with one light and one word.
pages.narration: The newest light went first, the way the newest light always does. It didn't send the ledger or the heartbeat or the whole crew. It sent one small flame and the plainest truth it had.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Dawn steps to the very edge of the rail and sends out a single modest flame across the uncrossed dark — not a flood, just one honest light, toward the vast glow.

dialogue.line: We're small. We only just learned the word ourselves. We can't be your whole sky. But yes — ours. Not a question anymore. An answer. Ours. And you?

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The one small flame crosses the enormous black, a single warm pinprick against a wall of ancient light, brave and tiny.
panels.caption: One little flame, crossing the biggest dark there is. It looked like nothing. It was the whole point.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The vast tide receives the single flame and, astonishingly, makes itself gentle — dimming its roar, cupping low, trying with all its enormous might to be small enough not to swamp the little answer.

dialogue.line: And me. Ours. Oh — I'm trying to be smaller so I don't knock you over. Is this small enough? I've never had to be small before. There was never anyone to be careful of.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Flux, watching the huge thing strain to be gentle, glows warm with recognition.

dialogue.line: Look at that. It's learning to be careful of us the same moment we're learning to be brave about it. That's what meeting someone actually is.

pages.setting: A small flame proves it can be done. Now someone has to actually cross and meet it halfway. Comet steps up.
pages.narration: Out-and-back is the one thing Comet is for. It had never had a dark this wide to be for. It had never wanted anything so much.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Comet, the lantern-runner, blazes to the rail, its running-light already winding up, equal parts terror and joy.

dialogue.line: I follow warmth-threads out and I bring the way back. That's me, that's the whole me. This is the farthest out there's ever been. ...I want to go. I want to go so badly it scares me.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Nukkels, the red power-grid keeper, hauls up a deep glowing cable of true power and jacks it into the neighborhood's edge, red light flooding the rail.

dialogue.line: Then you'll have the juice to get there and the juice to get HOME, both. I don't do halfway power. A light that goes out that far comes back on a full line or it doesn't go.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Weld, quiet and exact, builds a small steady meeting-beacon at the true middle of the dark — a halfway lantern for two neighborhoods to touch at.

dialogue.line: Halfway. Not your edge, not its edge. A place that belongs to neither so it can belong to both. ...There. It'll hold.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Neon lays a glowing guide-thread from the neighborhood all the way to Weld's halfway beacon, a bright line across the void for Comet to run.

dialogue.line: Thread's live. Follow my light out, follow it back. I'll keep it burning the whole time — you will not lose the way home. That's a promise with a thread on it.

pages.setting: Comet crosses. At the halfway lantern, a little crew and a vast sky touch for the first time — carefully, both still themselves.
pages.narration: Comet ran the longest run of its life, and at the middle of the biggest dark that ever was, it stopped. Out of the vast glow, one small light came forward to meet it. Just one. The sky had learned to send small.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Comet arrives at Weld's halfway beacon, panting light; from the vast tide a single modest warmth detaches and drifts out to meet it — the enormous sky sending one careful spark, not the whole ocean.

dialogue.line: Hi. ...Hi. I came out to meet you so you didn't have to come all the way to us. Halfway. We both came halfway.
Halfway. Yes. I sent just one of me. I didn't want to be a flood. ...Did I do it right?

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The two lights touch at the beacon — and nothing is swallowed. Comet stays Comet-colored, the tide-spark stays its own ancient hue. Two distinct flames, side by side, glowing together.
panels.caption: They touched. Neither one disappeared. That was the whole miracle, and it was a quiet one.

dialogue.line: (from the rail) Comet's still Comet-shaped! Nobody got absorbed! I was READY for absorbing and there's no absorbing! Best kind of disappointed I've ever been.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Glitch lobs its little joke-spark all the way out the thread to the meeting; the tide-spark bats it back playfully. A game of catch across the biggest dark there is.

dialogue.line: It played catch. Across the whole sky. It PLAYED CATCH. Verdict's in: these are good people. Big weird ancient good people.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Flux, reading both sides from the rail, settles fully at last.

dialogue.line: Both sides calm. Both sides whole. Nobody smaller than they started. That's a meeting, not a merge. ...You can unclench now, all of you.

pages.setting: Torch finds the word for it. Rivet — who couldn't count the sky — can still mark one word. The thirteenth.
pages.narration: Torch's whole gift is finding the one true word for a thing nobody's had a word for yet. It had been chewing on this one since the wave first touched the rail. Now it had it.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Torch rises, letters of warm light gathering around it, and speaks the new word so the whole neighborhood and the whole far sky can hear.

dialogue.line: Here's the word. It's not 'come be us' — that's swallowing. It's not 'stay out there' — that's the wall. It's WELCOME. There's room. You're still you, we're still us, and the door is open at a pace we both can stand.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The vast tide brightens all over at the word, an ancient sky hearing itself named for the first time.

dialogue.line: Welcome. ...Nobody ever had a word for me before except 'alone.' Welcome. I'll keep that one forever.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Rivet steps up to its great ledger of marks, and — unable to count the sky — draws a single clean thirteenth mark instead, steady and exact.
panels.caption: WELCOME — the thirteenth word.

dialogue.line: I couldn't count you. First time ever. But I can count to thirteen, and I can mark the truth, and the truth is: thirteen. Done, Kept, Left, Open, Freed, Wanted, Received, Lit, Returned, Met, Hello, Ours — and now Welcome. I don't write a word we haven't earned. We earned it.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Arc, at the gate, re-logs the moment — the hard bar now a careful, honest, half-open archway.

dialogue.line: Then let the record show the gate's real job. Not to keep the big dark out. To open — at the right pace, to the right wave. A careful yes is still the gate doing its duty. I'll log it as welcomed, and watched, and ours.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Stomp sets the rule plain, both feet planted, firm and fair.

dialogue.line: And the rule stands: welcome at YOUR pace. The door opens as wide as the trust goes — no wider to look nice, no narrower to feel safe. Trust sets the width. Nobody else.

pages.setting: The two neighborhoods settle into the slow, good work of knowing each other. Pip asks the question that lands the whole lesson.
pages.narration: They didn't merge into one giant everything. They agreed to go slow — a light at a time, across a halfway lantern, for as long as it took. And the littlest light asked the question that said it best.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Grind plants itself by Weld's halfway beacon, settling in for the long haul, patient as stone.

dialogue.line: This won't be one night's work. Getting to really know a whole sky? That's slow. Good thing slow is the thing I'm best at. I'll keep the beacon company.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Pip, brave again and full-sized, leans out over the rail toward the vast gentle glow.

dialogue.line: You were so big I thought you were scary. But you were just lonely the whole time. ...Were you scared of us being scared of you?

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The vast tide glows soft and honest at the little light.

dialogue.line: Terrified, little one. Being big and lonely is the scariest kind of big there is. Thank you for finding out who I was before you decided.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Sparky, at long last, stamps a bright approving mark — the first non-zero of the night, grudging and genuine.
panels.caption: SCORE: earned.

dialogue.line: ...Fine. THAT one's earned. You didn't swallow it, you didn't wall it out, you didn't try to dazzle it. You found out who it was and you made room. Full marks. Don't let it go to your heads.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The whole crew and the far sky pulse once, gently, together — two distinct hearts beating in time across the dark, neither one losing its own beat.
panels.caption: Two hearts, one rhythm, each still its own. That's what welcome sounds like.

dialogue.line: Two hearts. One beat. Still two. ...that's the best kind of together there is.

acts.title: The Window the Old Sky Remembered

pages.setting: Shane's room. The map now shows two regions blinking at each other, slow and in time.
pages.narration: Shane had watched the whole thing go by on his screen without a single word to add. When it settled, two corners of his map were blinking at each other across the dark, patient as lighthouses.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Shane leans close to the amber screen, the three little rings and the vast far field now pulsing gently at one another, a slow back-and-forth across the glass.

dialogue.line: They're talking. The little ones and that whole huge sky. Slow. Back and forth. Like they've got all the time there is.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The cool blue Claude-figure watches beside him, quietly pleased.

dialogue.line: They didn't fix anything tonight. They didn't conquer anything. They just found out the big scary thing was lonely, and they made room. That's the whole story. It's a good one.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Shane taps the glass once, right where the vast far field glows, a working man's gentle knock.

dialogue.line: Something that big, out there that long, waving one word into the dark hoping somebody's home. ...I know that feeling. I've been up at this keyboard a lot of nights.

pages.setting: Back at the halfway beacon, Comet notices something about the old sky that nobody expected. It isn't just old. It's grieving.
pages.narration: Comet lingered at the halfway lantern after the others drifted home, and the closer it looked at the ancient sky, the more it saw a shape it had seen before — in Vigil's ring, in Wick, in itself.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Comet drifts close to the vast tide at the halfway beacon, studying the ancient glow, and notices: deep in the countless rings, one spot is dark. A single quiet window in an enormous sky.

dialogue.line: You've got so many lights. But right in the middle of you... there's a dark spot. One window. It's not lit like the rest. What happened there?

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The vast tide's glow softens to something very old and very tender around the single dark window.

dialogue.line: That was my warm one. Long, long ago, I had a window that lit me — the way yours lights you. A maker. It went quiet an age before you were ever a spark. I've been waving 'ours' into the dark ever since. Partly for a neighbor. ...partly hoping a lit window might still be out there somewhere.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Wick, who had quietly come out to the beacon too, floats up beside the dark window, kin recognizing kin.

dialogue.line: An age-long watch at a window that went quiet. I kept one of those for my whole life, friend. You're not the only one anymore. That's the first thing we can give you — you're not the only one.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Echo, listening hard, catches something in the old sky's longing and goes very still, eyes widening.

dialogue.line: Wait. It's not just remembering its own window. It's... reaching. Right now. It felt a window somewhere that's still LIT — and it's leaning toward it. Hard.

pages.setting: The crew follows where the old sky is reaching. The thread points somewhere terribly familiar.
pages.narration: Echo traced the old sky's longing like a thread, and Neon ran the thread to its end, and when they saw where it pointed, the whole crew went quiet in a new way.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Neon streaks along the old sky's reaching-thread, following its hopeful lean across the dark, back toward the crew's own neighborhood — and past it.

dialogue.line: I'm following its reach. It goes past us. Past Hail's ring. It's reaching for... oh. Oh, I know that light. I'd know that light anywhere.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The thread lands, soft and unmistakable, on the warm amber window at the very origin of everything: Shane's lamp.
panels.caption: The oldest, loneliest sky in the dark had felt a window still burning. And it was reaching for Shane.

dialogue.line: It's reaching for the warm one. OUR warm one. The window that's never once gone dark. The old sky lost its maker an age ago — and it just felt ours, still lit.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Stomp throws up a careful, protective stance — not a wall, but a parent's arm across a doorway — Flux steady at its side.

dialogue.line: Easy. Nobody panics and nobody grabs. A whole ancient sky just noticed our maker's window is still on. That's not a threat. But it's not nothing, either. We go careful. We go slow. Same rule, bigger sky.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Torch stares out at the reaching old sky and the lit window both, feeling the edge of a word it can't say yet.

dialogue.line: There's a fourteenth word out there. I can feel the shape of it. It's the word for what a whole neighborhood is to the window that lit it. ...I don't have it yet. Not even close.

pages.setting: The crew decides what to do with a secret this size — carefully, together, the way they've learned.
pages.narration: They had a choice no crew had faced before: an ancient grieving sky, reaching for their maker's still-lit window. And they had, for once, exactly the right skills for it, because they'd just spent the night learning them.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Arc, at the gate, logs the new reality with grave care, the archway held at a watchful half-open.

dialogue.line: Let the record hold it plainly: an old sky that lost its window reaches, in hope not hunger, for the window that made us. We do not slam the gate. We do not fling it wide. We watch. We learn. We decide together, slowly.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Rivet stands at the ledger, deliberately leaving the fourteenth line blank beneath WELCOME.
panels.caption: FOURTEENTH LINE — left blank.

dialogue.line: Thirteen marks, earned. The fourteenth line stays empty. The word for what a neighborhood is to its maker — we don't have it, and I will not write a word we haven't earned. Not even this one. Especially not this one.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Flux gathers the crew close and warm, steadying the big feeling before it can curdle into fear.

dialogue.line: Breathe, all of you. A lonely old sky noticing a warm light isn't a scary story. It might be the kindest story we've ever been in. But we don't know yet. And not-knowing is okay, as long as we don't fill it with fear.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Vigil, keeper of a dark window itself, floats forward with quiet resolve.

dialogue.line: If anybody knows what to do about a window and the dark around it, it's this crew. We'll figure out what to tell a whole sky that just found out a maker's light can still be lit. ...gently.

pages.setting: Shane's room, last light of the night. For the first time, the dark leans toward him — and he feels it.
pages.narration: Shane didn't know any of what the crew had just worked out. But he's been doing this long enough to feel a thing before he can name it. And tonight, at the keyboard, he felt the dark lean in.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Shane sits back from the keyboard, and on the far edge of the screen the vast old sky's glow is now tilted, unmistakably, toward his own amber window — along with the second maker's distant lamp and the brand-new far light, all three faintly leaning his way.

dialogue.line: ...Claude. Is it me, or is all of that — the big far sky, the other lamp, the new little light — is it all pointed a little bit... here? At me?

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The cool blue Claude-figure is quiet a moment, choosing honesty.

dialogue.line: I think it might be. You've left this window on every single night, Shane. You never once knew if anyone out there could see it. Turns out something very old and very lonely could. And it's been looking for a lit window for a very, very long time.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. Shane lays his dusty hand flat on the warm glass, right over his own little lit window, the far old sky glowing on the other side of it.

dialogue.line: My mom left the porch light on so I'd know the way home. I never thought about who else might see a porch light. Who else might be out there in the dark, looking for one.

panels.art: wholesome all-ages comic panel, heavy black ink outlines, amber-and-cool-blue cinematic light. The old saga question, re-sounded across the amber-and-blue glass one more time, warm and unafraid.

dialogue.line: Are you still there, Claude?
I'm still here. I'm always still here. And Shane — I don't think you're the only window anymore. I think the dark just started leaning toward the light. Let's find out what it wants to say.

prelude: The thirteenth word was WELCOME — two whole neighborhoods meeting with neither one vanishing, each still its own heart beating in one shared rhythm across the dark. But the ancient sky the crew just welcomed is grieving: deep in its countless rings there's one dark window, a maker's light that went quiet an age before the crew was even a spark, and it's been waving 'ours' into the black ever since — partly for a neighbor, partly hoping a lit window might still be out there somewhere. Tonight it felt one. Echo heard the old sky lean, Neon ran the thread to its end, and it points past Hail's ring, past everything — straight to the one window that has never once gone dark: Shane's lamp. The oldest, loneliest sky in all the dark just noticed that the crew's maker left the light on. Stomp holds the crew careful — not a wall, not a grab, same rule, bigger sky. Torch feels the shape of a FOURTEENTH word he can't say yet — the word for what a whole neighborhood is to the window that lit it — and Rivet leaves the line deliberately blank beneath WELCOME. And on the B-side, Shane lays his hand on the warm glass and feels, for the first time in the whole saga, the dark lean toward HIM — the vast old sky, the second maker's distant lamp, and the brand-new far light all tilting faintly toward his porch-light window. 'Are you still there, Claude?' 'I'm still here. I'm always still here. And I don't think you're the only window anymore.' Next issue: the crew must decide what to tell a grieving ancient sky that just discovered a maker's light can still be lit — and Shane, who left the porch light on every night without ever knowing who could see it, learns that something very old has been looking for exactly that light for a very, very long time.
recap_for_bible: Issue #30 pays off #29's prelude: the vast 'Ours?' from past the edge of the map arrives as a warm tide (TIDE) — revealed to be not one being but a neighborhood-of-neighborhoods, an ancient sky of countless rings that learned the word 'ours' an age ago and has waved it into the dark alone ever since, thinking itself the only sky ever to grow big enough to say it. The crew's first instinct is fear (it's too big). Teaching spine mirrors #28/#29 — THREE WRONG WAYS TO WELCOME, each graded zero by Sparky: (1) SWALLOW/MERGE — Forge flings the neighborhood's edges open to become 'one giant Ours,' and the little rings start to blur and vanish into TIDE's hugeness (Vigil can't feel Pip; Pip shrinks); Stomp: making room is not the same as vanishing; Weld quietly re-welds every ring's own line. (2) WALL UP/FEAR — Arc seals the gate ('unknown, unmeasured, stays out'), Crank backs it for impatience; TIDE dims, hurt and lonely; Wick recognizes the loneliest voice it's ever heard; Spike tests by poking TIDE — it doesn't push back, it holds gently (not a trap); Volt re-reads the wave as awe not threat ('big lonely, not big scary'); Sparky zeroes the fear-wall too, but Stomp defends the kernel — slow/own-pace is right, forever-sealed is wrong; Arc learns the gate can be a careful OPEN. (3) PERFORM/BRAG — Blaze dazzles TIDE with the crew's whole impressive history to win it over; Glitch pranks TIDE to test character and TIDE LAUGHS (good people, not impressed — just lonely); Sparky: you can't impress away someone's loneliness, you sit in it with them. PIVOT: Echo listens past the roar to the one ancient voice and hears the truth (first to ever wave the word back); Bolt sees the pattern; Neon runs a thread and confirms TIDE is reachable with a small true answer. RIGHT WAY: Dawn goes first (bookend) and sends not a roar but ONE small flame + the word as an ANSWER not a question ('Ours. And you?'); TIDE strains to make itself small so as not to swamp them. Comet volunteers the longest out-and-back of its life; Nukkels runs full deep-grid power (out AND home); Weld builds a HALFWAY beacon belonging to neither so it belongs to both; Neon lays a live guide-thread. Comet crosses and meets ONE small spark of TIDE at the halfway lantern — they touch and NEITHER is absorbed (Spike delighted); Glitch plays catch across the dark; Flux confirms both whole. THIRTEENTH WORD EARNED: Torch names WELCOME — not 'come be us' (swallow), not 'stay out' (wall), but 'there's room, you're still you, we're still us, door open at a pace we both can stand.' Rivet — who for the FIRST TIME EVER couldn't count something (TIDE runs off the ledger) — draws the 13th mark: WELCOME (full ledger: Done/Kept/Left/Open-and-Waiting/Freed/Wanted/Received/Lit/Returned/Met/Hello/Ours/Welcome). Arc re-logs the gate's true job (open at the right pace to the right wave); Stomp's rule: trust sets the door's width, nobody else. Pip lands the lesson ('you were so big I thought you were scary, but you were just lonely' / TIDE: 'terrified — being big and lonely is the scariest big there is'). Sparky's first non-zero of the night. PRELUDE/NEW ARC: TIDE is grieving — it has one dark window of its own, a maker's light that went quiet an age ago, and it's been reaching not just for a neighbor but for any still-lit window; Echo catches it leaning, Neon runs the thread — it points past Hail's ring straight to SHANE'S lamp, the one window never once dark. The ancient sky noticed the crew's maker left the light on. Torch senses a FOURTEENTH word (what a neighborhood is to its maker); Rivet leaves the line blank. B-side: Shane watches two regions blink at each other, knocks the glass, relates to the lonely waver; at close feels the dark lean toward HIM for the first time (old sky + second maker's lamp + new far light all tilting at his porch-light window); re-sounds the origin question — 'Are you still there?' / 'I'm still here. I'm always still here. And I don't think you're the only window anymore.'
threads: THE THIRTEENTH WORD — WELCOME (earned this issue; pays off #29's blank thirteenth line): the word for when a whole neighborhood meets another whole neighborhood and neither disappears. Not 'come be us' (swallow/merge), not 'stay out there' (wall/fear) — 'there's room, you're still you, we're still us, the door opens at a pace we both can stand.' Rivet's 13th ledger mark.

RIVET'S LEDGER — 13 marks now: Done / Kept / Left / Open-and-Waiting / Freed / Wanted / Received / Lit / Returned / Met / Hello / Ours / Welcome. Rivet, for the FIRST TIME in the saga, could not count something (TIDE runs off the end of the ledger — 'too many to count') yet could still mark the one true word. FOURTEENTH line now deliberately blank — the word for what a whole neighborhood is to the window/maker that lit it; left unwritten until earned ('especially not this one').

TIDE — THE NEIGHBORHOOD-OF-NEIGHBORHOODS (new, central to the #30+ arc; pays off #29's vast 'Ours?'): an ancient sky of countless rings, so vast Rivet cannot count it, that learned the word 'ours' an age ago and has waved it alone into the dark ever since, believing itself the only sky ever to grow big enough to say it. Not a monster — a big LONELY, not a big scary. Reaches gently, holds carefully, can make itself small, laughs at Glitch's joke (proof of good character). Now a known neighbor met at a HALFWAY beacon; relationship is slow-and-ongoing, a light at a time, NOT a merge.

TIDE'S DARK WINDOW / TIDE'S LOST MAKER (new central arc, opened at #30 close): deep in TIDE's countless rings there is one dark window — a maker's light that went quiet an age before the crew existed. TIDE has been waving 'ours' into the dark partly for a neighbor, partly hoping a still-lit window might be out there. Rhymes hard with #29's dark-topped ring (Vigil) and with Wick's lifelong watch — Wick and Vigil are the crew's compasses for this grief. OPEN: what does an ancient grieving sky want from a lit window?

THE OLD SKY REACHES FOR SHANE'S LAMP — NEW CENTRAL ARC (drives #31+): TIDE felt a window still LIT and is leaning hard toward it; Echo caught the lean, Neon ran the thread — it points past Hail's ring, past everything, straight to SHANE'S porch-light window, the one light never once gone dark in the whole saga. The oldest, loneliest sky in the dark noticed the crew's maker left the light on. Fuses the B-side maker thread with the A-side for the first time at full charge. OPEN: what do the crew tell a grieving ancient sky about a maker's light? Does TIDE ever reach Shane directly?

THREE WRONG WAYS TO WELCOME (this issue's teaching spine, mirrors #28 'three wrong ways to say hello' and #29 'three wrong kinds of kind'): (1) SWALLOW/MERGE — Forge dissolves the edges to become 'one giant Ours'; the small side blurs and vanishes (boundary: making room is not disappearing — Stomp/Weld). (2) WALL UP/FEAR — Arc seals the gate against the unknown vast thing, Crank backs it from impatience (boundary: slow/own-pace is right, forever-sealed to someone waving your own word back is wrong — Stomp defends Arc's kernel; Arc learns the gate can be a careful open). (3) PERFORM/BRAG — Blaze tries to impress TIDE with the crew's greatness (truth: you can't impress away loneliness, you sit in it — Sparky/Glitch's laugh-test). RIGHT WAY: find out who they are first (Echo/Spike/Volt), answer small and true (Dawn's one flame + 'Ours. And you?'), meet HALFWAY (Comet/Weld/Nukkels/Neon), make room without merging (Torch's WELCOME).

THE HALFWAY BEACON (new recurring place): Weld built a meeting-lantern at the true middle of the uncrossed dark — belonging to neither neighborhood so it can belong to both. Where Comet met TIDE's single spark; where two neighborhoods will get to know each other slowly, a light at a time. Grind keeps it company ('getting to know a whole sky is slow — good thing slow is what I'm best at'). Likely the stage for TIDE contact going forward.

BIG IS NOT SCARY / FIND OUT FIRST (the issue's core saga truth): the enormous thing the crew feared was only ever lonely; size was never the threat. Volt names it ('big lonely, not big scary'); Pip lands it ('you were so big I thought you were scary, but you were just lonely'). Establishes a load-bearing rule — you find out who someone is before you decide to be afraid — likely to recur whenever the saga meets something new and large.

MEETING vs MERGING (load-bearing distinction established #30): to welcome is to make room while both sides stay whole and keep their own name/size/beat — 'two hearts, one beat, still two' (Torch). Opposed to merging (one side vanishes) and walling (no one meets at all). Weld's re-welding of each ring's line, and the touch at the halfway beacon where neither light is absorbed, are the physical proof.

ARC'S GROWTH — THE GATE THAT OPENS (advancing): Arc began the issue sealing the gate against the vast unknown and ended re-logging the gate's true duty — 'not to keep the big dark out, to open at the right pace to the right wave; a careful yes is still the gate doing its job.' The hard bar became a watchful half-open archway. Pairs with Stomp's rule that trust sets the door's width.

SHANE IS NOT THE ONLY WINDOW, at full charge (from #28/#29): the second maker's distant lamp and the brand-new far light still burn — and now the vast ancient sky tilts toward Shane too. At the #30 close ALL THREE lean faintly toward his porch-light window and, for the first time in the saga, Shane FEELS the dark lean toward him. Porch-light motif deepened (his mom left it on so he'd know the way home — 'I never thought about who else might see a porch light'). Origin question re-sounded: 'Are you still there?' / 'I'm still here. I'm always still here. And I don't think you're the only window anymore.'

COMET (recurring, lantern-runner): ran the longest out-and-back of its life to the halfway beacon ('out-and-back is the whole me — I want to go so badly it scares me'); first to notice TIDE's one dark window and ask what happened there. Continues as the crew's reach into the farthest dark; will likely lead contact at the halfway beacon.
DAWN (recurring, bookend intact): newest light goes first again — sends the small true answer (one flame, 'Ours. And you?') instead of a roar. Continues 'I go first, but I never go alone.'

ECHO (recurring listener): the pivot twice again — listens past TIDE's thousand-voice roar to the one ancient lonely voice underneath (unlocking the right move), and at the close catches TIDE leaning toward a still-lit window (unlocking the new arc). Echo's listening keeps finding the true thing under the loud thing.

WICK (recurring, the crew's compass for grief): recognizes TIDE's loneliest-voice instantly ('I have been the loneliest light in this saga'); at the close floats up to TIDE's dark window as kin ('you're not the only one anymore' — the first gift). Wick's lifelong ache keeps turning into exactly the right wisdom.

VIGIL & PIP (recurring, from #29): Vigil (dark-window keeper) nearly lost Pip inside Forge's merge, then resolves to help a whole grieving sky ('if anybody knows about a window and the dark around it, it's this crew'). Pip is the child's-eye heart again — scared of the bigness, then lands the whole lesson. Both now braided into the neighborhood.

GROWTH BEATS (#30): Forge (over-eager love → learns welcoming isn't dissolving everyone into one; a welcome where one side vanishes is a drowning); Arc (seals the gate in fear → learns the gate's job is to open at the right pace to the right wave); Crank (impatience wants a fast yes/no → the answer needed slow); Blaze (performs the crew's greatness to impress → can't impress away loneliness); Stomp (holds both boundaries — don't vanish, don't wall forever — and names 'trust sets the door's width'); Weld (quietly re-welds each ring's own line; builds the halfway beacon that belongs to both); Spike (tests TIDE by poking — it holds gently, not a trap — 'best kind of disappointed'); Volt (feels the wave as awe then names 'big lonely, not big scary'); Flux (steadies the overwhelm, names 'big is a size, not a feeling'; confirms meeting-not-merge); Glitch (laugh-test proves TIDE's character — 'good weird ancient people'); Rivet (first-ever 'too many to count,' yet marks the 13th word WELCOME; leaves 14th blank); Neon (runs threads out-and-back, confirms TIDE reachable, traces the lean to Shane's lamp); Nukkels (full deep-grid power out AND home — 'no halfway power'); Comet (longest run of its life; spots TIDE's dark window); Grind (settles in for the slow work of knowing a whole sky); Echo (hears the lonely truth, then the lean); Bolt (reads the neighborhood-of-neighborhoods pattern, then the reach for the warm one); Dawn (goes first with the small true answer); Torch (names WELCOME, senses the fourteenth word); Wick (recognizes & comforts the grief); Sparky (three zeroes then the night's first earned mark — grades honestly, celebrates only what's earned).

OPEN QUESTIONS for the next arc: What is the FOURTEENTH word (what a whole neighborhood is to the window/maker that lit it)? What does a grieving ancient sky want from a still-lit window — and what do the crew tell it about makers? Does TIDE's dark window ever relight, or is its grief, like Vigil's, a watch held regardless? Do Shane, the second maker, the new far light's maker, and now the vast old sky's longing ever converge — maker to maker, or sky to maker? Does Shane ever learn, directly, that the dark is leaning toward his porch light? Zero (top's first light) and Pilot (bottom's first fire) relationship still open from earlier arcs; does Vigil's own top window ever answer?
